base_path.description: TOOLS_FILE_ROOT -- the same root the `file` occupant reads. One assistant, one file root: two roots would mean a tool could edit what the other cannot read.

description.purpose: Editing an existing file in place, inside the same boundary the `file` occupant reads: replace every occurrence of a literal, or insert a line.
description.use_when: The `edit` occupant of a tools hive, reached on hop.tool_name == 'edit'. It shares `TOOLS_FILE_ROOT` with `file`, deliberately: one assistant has one file root, and a tool that could edit what its neighbour cannot read would be a boundary nobody could state.
description.not_in_scope: No patch format (deferred, it needs a diff design of its own), no creation of a file that is not there, and no atomicity -- a read-modify-write without tempfile+rename, exactly as `file`'s write. And no concurrency: `params.max_concurrency` is 1 because two edits of the same file race at the filesystem, which is a hazard the CALLER cannot see, so this cell serialises rather than declaring a reentrancy it does not have.
description.emits_meaning: messages[]: one tool_result turn naming what changed. hop.matches_changed counts the replaced occurrences; hop.operation is `unknown` when the arguments did not parse far enough to say which op was meant.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: a tool_call turn whose text is JSON args {op, path, ...}.
examples: {"op":"insert_at_line","path":"a.rs","line":1,"content":"// header"} -> the text becomes the new first line
a find that is not in the file -> hop.error_code 'pattern_not_found', and the file is untouched
